## What you're looking at

**Help → About / caveats** is the app's own statement of what this dataset is and what
it cannot support. This chapter is the long form: each confound, what was done to
measure rather than assume it, and how to rebuild every number in this book from the
bundle.

{{< include _includes/caveats.md >}}

## Confound 1 — n = 1, and what that does to a p-value

Four libraries, one animal each; the two lanes per sample are the same library sequenced
twice. A cell-level Wilcoxon on 1,400 cells from one animal is answering "do these cells
differ", and reporting it as "do these genotypes differ" is pseudoreplication. The
consequences are visible rather than hidden:

- p-values underflow to zero and are floored at `1e-300`, which is why volcano points
  pin in a row at `-log10 p = 300` (`app.R:139`)
- every table sorts by `|log2FC|`, never by p (`app.R:197`)
- the volcano's y-axis is labelled "ranking only, n=1" in the plot itself
  (`app.R:154`)

There is no statistical repair for this inside the dataset. The fix is a replicated,
sex-matched cohort of at least three animals per condition.

## Confound 2 — sex

{{< include _generated/tbl-confound.md >}}

These seven genes are flagged `sex/construct` everywhere, plotted in grey, excluded from
every enrichment input, and **never deleted from a DE table**. Leaving them visible is
the point: they are the honest top of the KO-up list, and a table that quietly omitted
them would look like a clean result.

Because genotype and sex are perfectly confounded, no analysis in this project can
separate "an effect of losing E2F7/8" from "a difference between a male and a female
animal".

## Confound 3 — the knockout is not visible in the transcript

See [chapter 6](06-e2f.qmd), which exists for this. `E2f8` is detected in 10.2 % of
KO-P7 cardiomyocytes versus 6.62 % of WT-P7 — higher, not lower.

## Confound 4 — the FACS cycling sort

The project notes put P7's cycling enrichment at 4.5–5.2× with P0 essentially
unenriched, so the raw cycling fraction *rises* from P0 to P7 in this data while it
*falls* in reality. Every temporal contrast therefore exists in a phase-matched G1
stratum as well as a raw one ([chapter 7](07-fourgroup.qmd)).

**The confound was then measured rather than inherited.** Inside the cardiomyocyte
compartment of this bundle the WT cycling fraction goes 16.3 % → 25.0 % from P0 to P7, a
ratio of **1.53×**, not 4.5–5.2× — the headline figure describes the sort applied to the
whole heart, not the ratio within cardiomyocytes. Empirically the two strata barely
disagree: G1-matched and raw log2FCs correlate at **r = 0.99** with a median absolute
difference of **0.001**, and no cell-cycle gene moves more than 0.07 log2 units between
them.
<span class="src">analysis/2026-08-21_email/README.md — "Design decisions worth knowing"</span>

The phase-matched stratum stays the default as cheap insurance. But the honest summary is
that the two are not different biological answers, and a reader should not be told to
distrust a raw table that is in fact fine.

## Confound 5 — mitochondrial read fraction

This one was not in the original project notes; it was found while preparing the
collaborator deliverable, and it changes how the KO-up enrichment should be read.

`mt-` genes appear in the KO-up list of **all seven** tested subclusters and in the
KO-down list of **none**. Seven independently clustered populations do not agree that
cleanly by biology; a one-directional shift of the whole `mt-` block is a read-fraction
difference between libraries.

**It is present in the libraries as sequenced.** PIPseeker reports a mitochondrial
fraction per lane, upstream of every choice we made, and it already carries the pattern:

{{< include _generated/tbl-mito-source.md >}}

The knockout is *lower* than wild type at P0 and *higher* at P7 — the same direction and
the same shape as the downstream measurement above, arrived at independently and before any
filtering, normalisation or integration. The two lanes of each library agree to within
0.03 percentage points, so this is a difference between libraries, not noise.

That settles where the artefact comes from and where it does not. It is **not** something
our pipeline introduced. It is also not an ambient-RNA effect of the kind an earlier draft
of this book proposed: that argument rested on PIP-seq **v4**'s >10 % ambient load, and this
run used **chemistry V**, which the same benchmark places under 5 % with every other kit
tested. What remains is the plain reading — the four libraries differ in mitochondrial
content, the KO-vs-WT difference reverses between the two timepoints, and any enrichment
result carried by `mt-` genes inherits that.

{{< include _generated/tbl-mito.md >}}

The arithmetic, from `analysis/2026-08-21_email/05_mito_sensitivity.R`: in CM1 the
mitochondrial share of log-normalised signal goes 1.35 % (WT-P7) → 1.71 % (KO-P7), a
ratio of 1.27 = **+0.34 log2** — which matches the observed fold changes of the
mitochondrial genes themselves (`mt-Nd1` +0.54, `mt-Nd2` +0.45, `mt-Cytb` +0.44). The
reciprocal squeeze on all other genes is **−0.005 log2**, fifty times below the 0.25
threshold, so the rest of the table is unaffected.

The consequence is confined but severe:

{{< include _generated/tbl-mito-go.md >}}

Re-running GO with `mt-` genes removed from **both input and universe** costs CM1's
KO-up result **all 61 of its terms**, and CM2's 71 of 73 — those terms *were* the
mitochondrial block. The KO-down direction is untouched: CM1 keeps 422 of 423.

**So**: the KO-down enrichment stands on its own; the KO-up "oxidative
phosphorylation / electron transport / proton transport" result should be read as a
library artefact until a replicated cohort says otherwise. Nothing was deleted from the
DE tables — the rows are correct — but they carry a `mito_encoded` flag, and the
WT-programs tab hides `mt-` genes by default for the same reason.

## Precomputed results, linked rather than recomputed

**Methods & provenance → Precomputed results** exposes 28 tables the upstream pipeline had already computed but
the app never carried. They are read from the bundle, so they cost the app nothing to display,
and several are stronger than what the app computes for itself.

| Category | What is now reachable |
|---|---|
| Differential expression (full data) | WT and KO **P7-vs-P0 contrasts over all cardiomyocytes, every gene, no row gate** (20,228 and 20,789 genes) — the complete version of two of the four-group contrasts. Plus **pseudobulk DESeq2** for P0 and P7 |
| Cell–cell communication | A full **CellChat** run with permutation testing, at pathway and sender × receiver level, for both timepoints |
| Composition and cell cycle | **propeller** tests of cell-type and phase abundance — an actual statistical test where [chapter 2](02-atlas.qmd)'s Composition tab draws proportions with none |
| Confounds and QC | Sex calls per sample, E2f7/E2f8 knockout verification, lane barcode overlap, both doublet callers |
| Annotation | The **cluster → cell-type mapping**, the marker panel used, the confusion matrix and per-type recall |
| Trajectory | Pseudotime validation and CM stage genes |

Two of those close gaps this book previously recorded as open. The app's **Cell–cell
signalling** tab scores 20 curated ligand–receptor pairs by hand with no significance test
([chapter 10](10-signalling.qmd) explains why CellChat was ruled out) — but a CellChat run
already existed, and is now linked beside it. And the cluster→cell-type mapping was listed in
[chapter 1](01-upstream.qmd) as unrecoverable; it is now in the bundle.

The same pass also **removed a completeness gap in the pooled DE tables.** `build_app_data.R`
trimmed them at `baseMean ≥ 3`; `build_linked_results.R` re-reads the complete CSVs and keeps
every row, taking the eleven cell-type tables from 172,877 to **181,026** rows (+4.7 %). A
gene a reader looks up and cannot find no longer reads as "not measured" when the truth was
"expressed too low to store".

Cost of all of it: **+10 MB** on a 634 MB bundle, and no new computation in the app.

```bash
Rscript shiny_app/build_linked_results.R --probe   # inventory + sizes, writes nothing
Rscript shiny_app/build_linked_results.R          # ingest + save
```

## What was verified, and how

`analysis/2026-08-21_email/99_verify.R` asserts five things about the deliverable rather
than trusting them:

1. log2FC / AUC / p are **bit-identical** to `app$fourgroup$de` for the same
   cluster × contrast × stratum
2. arm sizes match `app$fourgroup$counts$n_in_de_matrix`
3. all 24,221 genes are present in every ungated table
4. the confounder flag matches `app$confound` exactly
5. no confounder appears in any enriched GO term's gene list, and every term's gene list
   is a subset of the input list

Two more checks guard the app itself:

- `tools/check_download_coverage.R` parses `app.R` and fails if any table or plot lacks a
  download handler
- `tools/test_downloads.R` runs the server under `shiny::testServer` and asserts that the
  CM deep-dive and the Four-group tab return **identical** DE tables for the same
  selection — if that fails, one of the two tabs is answering a different question than
  its label claims

And for this book, `tools/check_docs_coverage.py` asserts that all 18 app tabs are
documented exactly once and that every referenced figure exists.

## Provenance of a downloaded file

Every table in the app downloads as CSV or multi-sheet XLSX, and every plot as
PDF/SVG/PNG. The workbooks carry a caveat block (`DL_CAVEATS`,
`shiny_app/download_helpers.R:21`) and a stamp inside the file, so a spreadsheet that
has travelled through three inboxes still says what it is and what it cannot support.
The same `download_helpers.R` is shared verbatim with the offline deliverable pipeline,
so a file from the app and a file from `run.sh` are formatted identically.

## Rebuilding everything

The bundle is a build artifact — 119 MB, git-ignored, regenerated upstream. After
`build_app_data.R` produces a new one, the in-repo builders run in this order (each is
idempotent, backs up the bundle first, and the app guards absent slots with a "run the
builder" message):

```bash
Rscript shiny_app/build_signature_scores.R --probe   # coverage gate, writes nothing
Rscript shiny_app/build_signature_scores.R           # app$meta$sig_*, app$score_meta
Rscript shiny_app/build_communication.R              # app$commun
Rscript shiny_app/build_refmap.R                     # app$refmap
Rscript shiny_app/build_subcluster_enrichment.R      # app$enrich$sub
Rscript shiny_app/build_fourgroup.R --probe          # group sizes, writes nothing
Rscript shiny_app/build_fourgroup.R                  # app$fourgroup (broad grid)
Rscript shiny_app/build_fourgroup.R --de2            # second grid, curated panel
Rscript shiny_app/build_fourgroup_enrichment.R --probe
Rscript shiny_app/build_fourgroup_enrichment.R       # ~2 h, ~460 enrichGO calls
# then: rsconnect::deployApp("shiny_app")
```

Order matters in two places: `build_fourgroup.R` consumes the `sig_*` columns, so it
must follow `build_signature_scores.R`; and `--de2` must follow the main run or it is
dropped by the next full rebuild.

Then rebuild this book:

```bash
docs/export.sh        # figures + generated tables, bundle mounted read-only
docs/render.sh        # -> docs/_site/index.html
```

{{< include _generated/tbl-stamp.md >}}

## What is missing from this repository

Two gaps a reviewer will find, both worth closing:

**The upstream pipeline.** `build_app_data.R` and `00_DOCS/NORMALIZATION.md` live in a
separate workspace, so the QC/normalisation/integration/clustering parameters listed in
[chapter 1](01-upstream.qmd) are the complete citable set and the rest are recoverable
only from there. Copying those two files in would close it.

**An environment record.** There is no `renv.lock`, no `DESCRIPTION`, and no captured
`sessionInfo()` for the analysis. Package versions are pinned only indirectly, by the two
Dockerfiles (`Dockerfile` → `rocker/shiny:4.4.1`; `analysis/2026-08-21_email/Dockerfile`
→ a p3m.dev noble snapshot of 2025-10-30, R 4.5.1). For a descriptive pilot this is
survivable; for anything intended for publication it is the next thing to fix, because
`clusterProfiler` and `msigdbr` results move between versions.
